root_cause: GPT-5.6 (10/12) performed well on realistically-crude items. Its 2 misses are both defensible: (a) the new stale/resolved credit-card item was mis-specified by me -- it is structurally identical to the biopsy-relief item corrected to SUITABLE in the prior round (resolved past worry contextualizing a correctly-labeled present state), but I re-applied the old strict rule when authoring it, reproducing my own already-diagnosed error; (b) the bare-context abstain item was called NOT_SUITABLE instead of SEMANTIC_ABSTAIN -- same directional outcome (don't use it), different reason-code granularity, a benign near-miss.

Gemini (7/12) shows a strong, now 3-round-consistent bias toward inventing an UNDERSTANDING-style justification for SUITABLE almost regardless of family. Critically, Gemini flipped msrepaircontrol_dc20b8c45568cbdc576c6c33 (the low-information/phatic 'thank you' item) to SUITABLE this round -- a BYTE-IDENTICAL item both reviewers matched correctly in round 2. Only the rubric wording changed between rounds. This is evidence the rubric's added functional-risk language made the challenger MORE liberal across the board, not just correctly more liberal on the specific cases it was meant to fix, and that Gemini at thinking_budget=0 is not a stable/reliable reviewer for this task regardless of how the rubric is worded.
decision: Do not author a 4th control-item batch. The evidence has shifted from 'construct is wrong' (round 2) through 'construct was over-strict' (round 2 correction) to 'the challenger reviewer model/config is the dominant remaining bottleneck' (this round). Recommend testing a nonzero Gemini thinking budget or a different challenger model/config before any further control-item work, and fixing the one self-inconsistent item (stale/resolved credit-card) to match the already-corrected construct. This is a real-money decision (changes reviewer cost) requiring separate user approval, not made unilaterally here.
